class.name: PhysXBlastAsset
class.brief_description: A fractured mesh, ready to drive a [PhysXDestructible3D].
class.description: Produced by the editor's [b]Fracture with Blast...[/b] dialog (right-click a [MeshInstance3D] in the Scene tree dock or a [Mesh] in the FileSystem dock), or by [PhysXBlastAuthoring] for scripted or offline authoring, and saved as a normal [code].tres[/code]/[code].res[/code] file next to the scene. Assign it to a [PhysXDestructible3D]'s [member PhysXDestructible3D.blast_asset] to use it -- there's nothing to configure on the asset itself once it's authored.

method.name: cook_hulls
method.description: Cooks every chunk's collision hull with this build and stores it in [member chunk_hulls], with [member hull_format]. The pieces and how they break stay the same. Fracturing already does this; use it for an asset fractured before hulls were stored, or whose hulls are out of date (see [method get_hull_status]). The asset's Inspector has a [b]Cook Hulls[/b] button that does the same. Returns [constant FAILED] if no hull could be cooked.

method.name: get_chunk_count
method.description: Returns how many chunks this asset has, including chunk [code]0[/code] (the whole unfractured mesh) -- so this is always one more than the number of pieces a full fracture actually produces.

method.name: get_hull_status
method.description: Whether this build can use the stored hulls: [constant HULLS_COOKED] if so, [constant HULLS_NONE] if there are none, [constant HULLS_OUT_OF_DATE] if they were cooked by another PhysX version (or without the GPU data a GPU build needs), or don't match the chunks. Without usable hulls, a [PhysXDestructible3D] cooks each chunk's hull when it first breaks off, as before; it shows a warning in the editor until they're cooked.

members.member: The raw NvBlast asset data (bond/chunk support-graph structure) -- a single relocatable memory block per NvBlast's own design, stored here as-is. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

Each chunk's collision hull, cooked ahead of time from its [member chunk_points]: one [PackedByteArray] per chunk, empty where a chunk had too few points to cook. A break only loads these, where it would otherwise cook each hull on the main thread (for example 41 ms down to 12 ms for eight 13-chunk spheres broken at once). They add roughly 6-35% to a text asset's size. Empty in an asset fractured before these were kept; see [method cook_hulls]. Not meaningful to edit by hand.
For each chunk, the index in its [member chunk_points] where its interior (cut) faces start. The faces of the source mesh come first. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

Per-chunk vertex normals, one [PackedVector3Array] per chunk, aligned with [member chunk_points]. Empty in an asset fractured before these were kept: fracture the mesh again to get them. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

Per-chunk render-mesh triangle-soup positions, in the source mesh's local space -- one [PackedVector3Array] per chunk, index-matched to [member asset_bytes]' own chunk indices. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

For each chunk, a [PackedInt32Array] with one entry per source surface: the index in its [member chunk_points] where that surface's faces start, in surface order, before the interior faces (see [member chunk_interior_starts]). Empty in an asset fractured before every surface was kept, where all the source faces are the first surface's. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

Per-chunk vertex UVs, one [PackedVector2Array] per chunk, aligned with [member chunk_points]. Empty in an asset fractured before these were kept: fracture the mesh again to get them. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

Which build cooked [member chunk_hulls]: the PhysX version, followed by [code]gpu[/code] when the hulls carry the data GPU dynamics needs (for example [code]PhysX 5.10.0 gpu[/code]). A GPU build uses only hulls with that data; a CPU build uses either.

The source mesh's material for each of its surfaces, [code]null[/code] where a surface had none. A [PhysXDestructible3D] draws each surface's faces with its material, and the cut faces with the first one unless [member PhysXDestructible3D.interior_material] is set. [member PhysXDestructible3D.material_override] replaces them all. The [b]Fracture with Blast[/b] dialog stores the [MeshInstance3D]'s surface override materials here where it has them. Empty in an asset fractured before these were kept.

constants.constant: The asset has no stored hulls.
The stored hulls are usable by this build.
The stored hulls can't be used by this build (another PhysX version, missing GPU data, or not one per chunk); they're cooked at runtime instead.
